extracted.intended_audience: SEC staff, exchange personnel, market participants (Members, vendors), and public commenters on exchange fee filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evidentiary criteria an exchange uses in an SEC rule filing to justify proposed connectivity and port fees (cost allocation, competitive comparison, anti-discrimination, projected revenue). Intended to show fees are reasonable, equitably allocated, and consistent with the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allocation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange did not allocate any of its expenses in full to any core services and did not double-count any expenses; instead it allocated applicable cost drivers across its core services using the same Cost Analysis as the basis for multiple proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate expenses proportionally across core services based on identifiable cost drivers; avoid assigning full costs to a single service or double-counting. Use the same underlying analysis consistently across related filings (e.g., connectivity and market data filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human resources expense allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate personnel costs to services based on the focus and job functions of employee groups (example: network infrastructure personnel allocated 48.5% to 10Gb ULL connectivity, 5.4% to Full Service MEO Ports, remainder to other services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify employee groups dedicated to particular functions and allocate a high percentage of those employees' costs to the relevant service; allocate smaller percentages across wider personnel groups when functions are not primary or full-time. Provide numerical allocations and explain rationale (e.g., 27.3% of personnel costs to 10Gb ULL, 6.9% to Full Service MEO Ports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation and amortization allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate depreciation and amortization expense to core services in amounts reflecting actual equipment and infrastructure used to provide those services (example: approximately 64.6% allocated to connectivity services: 61.3% to 10Gb ULL physical connections and 3.3% to Full Service MEO Ports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what assets (servers, monitors, storage, network switching infrastructure, security appliances) underlie depreciation allocations and justify why only a portion of total depreciation is attributed to connectivity rather than all of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocated shared expenses (general overhead)
rubrics_metrics.description: Portions of general shared expenses (office space and expenses, utilities, recruiting and training, marketing and advertising, professional fees, telecommunications, director compensation) are allocated to Full Service MEO Ports as part of overall costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List included shared expense categories, state allocation percentages (e.g., 3.0% to Full Service MEO Ports; directors' cost allocated less than 4% to ports), and explain the weighting methodology (costs weighted to each Core Service based on understanding of each area's attributable costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of double-counting in cost analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange did not allocate any expenses in full to any core services and did not double-count expenses; applicable cost drivers were allocated across core services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the allocation approach and provide examples showing the same expenses are not claimed multiple times across services; explain how shared resources are split among services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate cost-per-unit calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute per-unit cost by dividing total monthly cost allocated to a service by the number of chargeable units (example: $165,793 monthly allocated to Full Service MEO Ports divided by 25 chargeable ports = approx $6,632 per month per port).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use projected-period data (here, projected 2024) and the number of chargeable units at the time pricing was determined; show the arithmetic and assumptions (number of chargeable ports, bulk vs single).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projected revenue vs. cost and profit margin disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide estimated annual cost and projected revenue for each service and compute resulting profit margin (example: 10Gb ULL annual cost $15,593,990 vs revenue $15,714,000 → 0.8% profit; Full Service MEO Ports cost $1,989,497 vs revenue $2,016,000 → 1.3% margin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that revenue estimates are projections contingent on customer behavior; disclose margins and assert they are modest, and explain that projections may be higher or lower in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive price comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare proposed fees to similar fees charged by competing exchanges to show fees are comparable or lower (examples: Exchange proposes $13,500/month for 10Gb vs Nasdaq $15,000 and NYSE American $22,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific competitor fee examples and use them to support the reasonableness of proposed fees; argue comparability regardless of small differences in profit margins across exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable allocation / not unfairly discriminatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are reasonable, fair, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory because they align with services provided, apply equally to all subscribers, and reflect relative resource consumption (e.g., 10Gb users consume >99% of message traffic and thus drive most network costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show usage statistics and resource-consumption differences between user types (10Gb vs 1Gb) to justify differential pricing; explain that fees apply uniformly (no favoritism) and are tied to consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered pricing rationale for Full Service MEO Ports
rubrics_metrics.description: Tiered pricing is used because Members who reach higher tiers consume the most bandwidth and network resources; tiers set fees to relate to the number of connections a firm purchases (more connections → greater resource use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supporting data (e.g., highest tier Market Makers account for >84% of ADV, lowest tier <14%) and describe package offerings (two ports per matching engine, up to 24 ports) with example per-port cost calculations under different fee levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of bundled port packages vs per-port charging
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange offers Full Service MEO Ports as a package (providing up to two Full Service MEO Ports per matching engine for a single monthly fee) rather than charging strictly on a per-port basis as other exchanges do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the package structure, show how effective per-port cost is calculated given matching engine count (e.g., $5,000/month divided by 24 = $208.33 per port), and note historical continuity (fee unchanged since 2018).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of intra-market competition/burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed fees will not impose an intra-market burden because they are uniform, reflect resource usage, and were developed after informal discussions with a diverse group of market participants; availability of third-party providers mitigates any potential disadvantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain outreach to participants (large/small firms, extranets, service bureaus), note that some participants may reduce/discontinue use (and provide example of one Market Maker terminating membership), and argue that the pricing does not impose barriers to entry for smaller participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of inter-market competition/burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange does not believe the fee change will impose an undue inter-market burden; without the fee the Exchange could be disadvantaged relative to others, and fees are a technology-driven change to recover costs and remain competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference comparable filings (e.g., Cboe) and Commission statements recognizing competition and the ability of competitors to meet demand if an exchange exits; argue that substitutable products and services are available and purchasers’ choices are voluntary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optionality and voluntariness of purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchasing additional ports or certification logical ports is voluntary and not required to participate in the production environment; exchanges may charge for optional excess certification ports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Cboe rationale and other exchanges' practices; emphasize that one free certification port per type remains and additional ports may be charged because they are optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to periodic review and update
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange commits to conduct a one-year review after fee implementation and periodic reviews thereafter; if revenue fails to cover costs or materially exceeds projections, Exchange may propose fee increases or decreases with updated cost estimates included in filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State timing (one-year review), decision triggers (revenues not covering costs or mark-up materially exceeding projections), and that updated cost estimates will be included in subsequent rule filings proposing fee changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of network architecture and technical differences to explain cost variance
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in technical architecture (e.g., number of matching engines: Exchange maintains 12 vs MIAX 24) and market model differences explain why profit margins and cost allocations may differ across affiliated exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that differing product offerings, pricing models, subscriber counts, and maturity phase affect costs and margins; argue that Commission staff should consider these differences when assessing profit margins and apply determinations consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification based on value provided (network performance and support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are justified because they allow the Exchange to cover costs of providing and maintaining hardware, network infrastructure, monitoring and support services that enable nanosecond-granularity performance and continuous improvement—services subscribers expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the operational benefits (performance, monitoring, improvement activities), tie these to the five primary revenue sources (transaction fees, connectivity, membership/regulatory fees, market data), and argue that fees reflect the value delivered to subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about projection limitations and business risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue projections are conditional; the Exchange acknowledges it may not realize projected revenues (depends on retaining/obtaining clients) and that use of connectivity services could decrease, affecting the ability to cover costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose business risk, state that pricing decisions should not be based solely on projections, and explain the intended use of projections—to confirm absence of supra-competitive profits—rather than as definitive guarantees.
